sentences.text: Prakash Bairwa vs Narayan on 11 March, 2025

Author: Gurpal Singh Ahluwalia
Bench: G. S. Ahluwalia
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Gwl:6191
 1 M.Cr.
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At G Wa L I O R
 Before
Hon'Ble
Shri Justice G. S. Ahluwalia

On The 11th Of March, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 6469 of 2025
 Prakash Bairwa
 Versus
 Narayan
 Appearance:
 Shri Prashant Chauhan - Advocate for applicant.
None for respondent.

Order 
This application, under Section 482 of CrPC / Section 528 of B.N.S.S. 2023, has been filed against the order dated 17.10.2024 passed by Additional Sessions Judge, Sheopur (M.P.), in Criminal Revision No.42 of 2023, arising out of order dated 10.06.2022 passed by Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Sheopur (M.P.), in Unregistered Complaint Case No.130 of 2022.

2. Facts, necessary for disposal of the present application, in short, are that complainant filed a complaint against respondent alleging that he had alienated his property and the consideration amount was lying with him.

The respondent approached him and instigated that he may give Rs.Five lacs and he would prepare an FDR of GCA in the name of complainant and his wife, and after 7 years, he would receive double of the amount.

The complainant was also verbally assured that in case if the company refuses to return the amount, then he NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:6191 (respondent) would return the same as he is in government job.
Accordingly, complainant gave Rs.2 lacs for preparing an FDR in the name of his wife and also gave Rs.3 lacs for preparing an FDR in his name.

Later on, when complainant asked the respondent to repay double of the amount, then respondent replied that he can only refund Rs.5 lacs as the company was running in losses and also assured that he would return the principal amount within one to one and a half months.

On 25.04.2022, when applicant demanded his money back, then Prakash Bairwa vs Narayan on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53822840/
1 respondent refused to return the principal amount also.
Accordingly, the complaint was made for offence under Section 420 of IPC.

The trial court dismissed the complaint after recording statements of witnesses by holding that the police had also submitted a report that the agents of the company, including the wife of respondent,
filed a complaint against the company, and under these circumstances, it was held that no prima facie case is made out to take cognizance against respondent.
Being aggrieved by the said order, applicant preferred a revision, which too has been dismissed on the ground that the police, in its report, had given a specific finding that it was the wife of the accused who was working as an agent of GCA Marketing Private Limited and she was depositing the amount in the scheme and the property of the company has also been seized.
Applicant had got the FDR prepared in the name of himself and his wife through the wife of the respondent.
Thus, prima facie, it was submitted that it was the wife of the respondent who got the FDR prepared, and the property of the company has also been seized.
3. It is submitted by counsel for applicant that since verbal assurance was given by respondent,
therefore, a prima facie case is made out against respondent.

4. Heard learned counsel for applicant.
5.
It is true that the amount of applicant was deposited in the company which NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:6191 had no license to run a non-banking business.
However, the only question for consideration is as to whether it was respondent who persuaded the complainant to get the FDR prepared, or it was the wife of the respondent?
6. Applicant has not impleaded the wife of respondent as an accused.

Had it been a case where the main accused i.e. Santara Bai, wife of respondent, has been implicated along with respondent, then it could have been said that at the instigation of respondent, the amount was invested in the company through the wife of respondent.

However, the main accused i.e. the wife of respondent,
who had invested money by acting as an agent, has not been impleaded as an accused.
In absence of main accused, the conspirator cannot be prosecuted in order to prove the offence of conspiracy.
Furthermore, the matter is under inquiry by the police, and even otherwise, Section 210 of CrPC (Section 233 BNSS, 2023) would also come in way of the complaint.
7. Accordingly, no case is made out warranting interference.
The application fails and is hereby dismissed.

(G.S. Ahluwalia) Judge pd Prakash Bairwa vs Narayan on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53822840/
